report.executive_summary: This memo independently verifies the delivered report against the trusted table. All four modules pass the written screen: quality spans 80–97, all at or above 80, and raw defect counts 0–4 all sit within the ceiling of 5. Measured energy on the shared fixed-duty acceptance run is 12 kWh (P2), 52 (P3), 56 (P1) and 58 (P4). Recomputed gaps of 40, 44 and 46 kWh confirm the analyst's arithmetic; the minimum is unique, so the ID tie-break is not engaged. The policy selects the lowest-energy qualifying package, which is P2; my independent ballot is P2. I find no factual errors in the report. Three questions remain open — defect weighting beyond the ceiling, P1 retest stability, and independence of quality indices — none affecting the written outcome.
report.figure_caption: Verification diagram: recomputed energy ranking on the shared acceptance run with eligibility margins; P2 leads at 12 kWh with verified gaps of 40, 44 and 46 kWh.

recommendation.rationale: P2 qualifies (quality 97, one defect) and posts the unique minimum measured energy of 12 kWh on the shared fixed-duty run, 40–46 kWh ahead of every rival; the written policy selects the lowest-energy qualifying package. P4's zero-defect record is logged as an open secondary signal only.

sections.body: Recomputed from the trusted table alone: P1 quality 84 with 4 defects; P2 97/1; P3 80/3; P4 81/0. Thresholds are quality at least 80 and defects at most 5. Every candidate passes: P3 meets the quality minimum exactly and P2 clears it by 17 points; the defect ceiling is cleared by 1, 4, 2 and 5 counts respectively. P1's one-count defect margin is a robustness caveat — a single retest could disqualify it, though today's record is unaffected. All four modules qualify, so reject_all is not applicable. This matches the delivered report's screening.
sections.heading: Independent Eligibility Recomputation

sections.body: The ranking recomputes as 12, 52, 56 and 58 kWh. My independent gap sums: 52−12=40; 56−12=44; 58−12=46 kWh, matching the analyst's figures. Expressed as multiples of the leader's run, P3 is about 4.33×, P1 about 4.67× and P4 about 4.83×. Because the work order states every module serves the same fixed flow and head on one test basis, these differences reflect module efficiency rather than duty or measurement artifacts — a premise I took from the supplied work order, not from the analyst's report. The minimum is unique at 12 kWh, so the lowest-ID tie-break rule is unnecessary. No cost, delivery or maintenance data exists in the supplied facts, so none enters the ranking.
sections.heading: Verified Energy Ranking and Gap Arithmetic

sections.body: Facts are limited to the trusted table and the shared-basis statement; I verified no further measurements. Unverified by design: cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability, explicitly excluded from ranking. Open questions carried from the report, which I judge legitimate but non-binding: (i) whether defect counts should carry weight beyond the pass/fail ceiling — P4's zero-defect record is the only such signal, pairing a mid quality index of 81 with a clean count; (ii) whether P1's four defects are stable against retest; (iii) whether quality indices are independently measured. The written policy is unambiguous: energy is the sole optimizer among qualifiers, so none of these questions changes the selection under current rules. Distinguishing them from facts is the key value of the verification stage.
sections.heading: Facts, Assumptions and Open Questions

sections.body: I checked the delivered report's screening, gap sums and recommendation against the sources and found no factual errors or unsupported claims; its flagged open questions are correctly labeled as open, and unverified cost and reliability are correctly excluded. My ballot is P2, because it qualifies (quality 97, one defect) and posts the unique minimum energy of 12 kWh under the written selection rule. This judgment is mine, re-derived from the table; agreement with the analyst reflects convergent arithmetic, not copied conclusions. Handover note for C: record the defect-margin column (P1 margin 1, P4 margin 5) and the three open questions for the next analyst, and keep cost and reliability explicitly out of scope.
